_doc: HMTc Category 20 (Oral Care) compiler config. Method v2.0, government-limit-only initial setting. The category splits into TWO instrument families with two different native bases that are never mixed. (1) FORMULATED oral products (dentifrices, mouthwash/oral rinse, cosmetic-presentation breath fresheners, whitening systems, denture and appliance care, and the residual 'other' row) are cosmetics on the oral mucosa that are partly swallowed. Their instrument family is the sovereign FINISHED-COSMETIC contaminant schedule on a total-content, as-placed-on-market basis, and the binding instrument throughout is Germany BVL 2017 — the only register instrument that publishes a separate, stricter TOOTHPASTE tier (Pb 500, Cd 100, tAs 500, tHg 100 ug/kg) alongside its general-cosmetic tier. The dentifrices row takes that tier as DIRECT regulatory alignment; the other formulated rows take the general-cosmetic tier directly where it is identical (Cd, tAs, tHg) and read the stricter toothpaste tier across for LEAD, disclosed as read-across, on the Category 15 precedent that the toothpaste tier is the closest regulated analogue for mucosal contact. (2) ARTICLES (toothbrushes, floss and interdental cleaners, oral irrigators and tips, tongue scrapers) are not cosmetics and a finished-cosmetic impurity limit does not reach them. Their instrument is Canada SOR/2018-83, the Consumer Products Containing Lead Regulations, which apply to a consumer product brought into contact with the user's mouth in normal use and cap EACH ACCESSIBLE PART at 90 mg/kg total lead; every other analyte on an article row is a component-level CONTROL because no sovereign sets a content limit for it. EN 71-3 / Directive 2009/48 toy values are migration limits and are excluded by the article basis guard. Colour-additive and ingredient purity specifications (21 CFR 73/74, the India permitted-colours entry) are excluded by the formulated basis guard: they cap one raw material, not a finished product. No number in this config is occurrence-derived, and no number is written into the config directly — every value resolves from a named row of data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv. Allowed provenance tags: regulatory-alignment, read-across, not-material, control.

_category.name: Oral Care
_category.anchor: sovereign finished-cosmetic contaminant schedules with the Germany BVL 2017 TOOTHPASTE tier as the oral-mucosal anchor for formulated products, and Canada SOR/2018-83's mouth-contact accessible-part lead ceiling as the article anchor
_category.basis_family: two declared bases, never mixed — (a) formulated oral products: finished product as placed on market, total content ug/kg as sold; (b) oral-care articles: total content per accessible part, ug/kg of that component's material. Neither basis is a dietary maximum level and neither is a migration/leachate value
_category.method_label: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default), Category 20 Oral Care: a formulated oral product takes the strictest applicable sovereign finished-cosmetic contaminant maximum in its as-sold basis, with the Germany BVL 2017 toothpaste tier read across to non-toothpaste oral-mucosal forms where it is stricter; an oral-care article takes the Canadian mouth-contact accessible-part lead ceiling and is otherwise held under component-level control. Species never replace totals, no ingredient purity specification anchors a finished-product cell, no migration value anchors a content cell, and no cell is occurrence-derived.
_category.method_note: Two boundary decisions in this category are disclosed rather than assumed. FIRST, breath fresheners split by presentation: the row certifies cosmetic-presentation forms (sprays, strips, films, non-food oral tablets) on the cosmetic instrument family, and food-presented mints, gums and confectionery lozenges are routed out to Category 33 rather than certified against a cosmetic ceiling — the relevant food instrument (the FDA lead action level for candy likely to be frequently consumed by small children, 100 ug/kg) is five times stricter than this category's lead value, so the routing is in the protective direction. SECOND, articles are not stretched onto cosmetic limits: a toothbrush, a floss, an irrigator tip and a tongue scraper each take a real article-scoped sovereign lead ceiling and a full-panel component-level control, and never a toothpaste value. Total chromium is a control rather than a published screen value in every row because no sovereign publishes a chromium content limit for any product form in this category; hexavalent chromium is deliberately NOT registered as a method artifact here, because oral-care matrices routinely contain peroxide and persulfate oxidising systems in which the reduction of Cr(VI) to Cr(III) cannot be assumed. Tin and aluminium are controls with declaration reconciliation rather than impurity ceilings, because stannous fluoride is an authorised active and hydrated alumina is a conventional abrasive, so both elements are present by design in compliant products.
_category.credible_note: The default HMTc credible set is the food-maximum-level regulator set, and it does not write this category's instrument family: neither the EU, Codex, FSANZ nor the UK publishes a numeric heavy-metal impurity schedule for cosmetics (Regulation (EC) 1223/2009 states a technically-unavoidable-traces principle with no table), so a category confined to the default set would have no anchors at all. The set is therefore widened to the sovereign COSMETIC regulators, each of which is a national competent authority publishing an enforceable finished-cosmetic contaminant schedule: Germany (BVL 2017, the tier that binds throughout and the only one with a toothpaste-specific row), Washington State (Toxics-Free Cosmetics Act, the only other toothpaste-specific instrument), Korea MFDS (the only cosmetic nickel and antimony limits anywhere in the register), China NMPA, Taiwan MOHW, the ASEAN Cosmetic Directive and its Indonesian, Malaysian, Singaporean and Thai transpositions, Kenya KS 2937, India Cosmetics Rules 2020, and EAEU TR CU 009/2011. Widening the set widens the AUDIT SCAN as well as the anchor pool, so every one of these instruments is checked for a stricter unselected value on every numeric cell. No addition changes a binding value except by making it stricter.

dentifrices.name: Dentifrices (toothpaste, gel, powder, tablets)
dentifrices.native_basis: finished dentifrice as placed on market (total content, ug/kg as sold)
dentifrices.native_basis_label: finished oral-care product as placed on market — total heavy-metal content per unit mass of product as sold (ug/kg). Not a dietary maximum level and not a migration/leachate value.
dentifrices.scope_note: Toothpastes, tooth gels, tooth powders and chewable or dissolving toothpaste tablets for adults and the general population, including fluoride dentifrices marketed under an OTC drug monograph: the taxonomy's first boundary rule routes by exposure pathway (oral cavity) and not by regulatory classification, so a monograph anticaries claim does not move the product out of this row. Children's dentifrices for ages 0-5 route to Category 2 (Infant and Child Personal Care) and that row must be at least as strict as this one. Dedicated whitening systems (peroxide strips, gels, trays, pens) route to the whitening-products row; a whitening CLAIM on a conventional dentifrice keeps the product here. This is the only row in the category that a sovereign toothpaste-specific instrument directly regulates.

dentifrices.basis_guard_note: Every named anchor on a formulated oral row must be a FINISHED-COSMETIC (or finished oral-product) total-content instrument. The guard rejects three families that would otherwise conflate bases: colour-additive and ingredient purity specifications (21 CFR 73/74, the India permitted-colours entry), which cap one raw material and not the finished product; migration/leachate values (EN 71-3 / Directive 2009/48 toy migration, food-contact migration), which measure release rather than content; and dietary maximum levels expressed as-consumed or wet weight. A basis failure resolves the cell to a GAP and fails the build rather than publishing a number in the wrong basis.

Pb.label: Germany BVL 2017 publishes a toothpaste-specific technically-avoidable lead content of 0.5 mg/kg, four times stricter than its own general-cosmetic tier (2 mg/kg), because a dentifrice sits on the oral mucosa and is partly swallowed. It is the strictest applicable sovereign value for this exact cell; the only other toothpaste-specific instrument, Washington State's Toxics-Free Cosmetics Act, is 1 mg/kg.
Pb.basis_label: finished dentifrice as placed on market (total lead content, ug/kg as sold)
Pb.substantiation: Germany BVL 2017 is the only instrument in the register that publishes a SEPARATE, STRICTER toothpaste tier alongside its general-cosmetic tier, and Washington State's Toxics-Free Cosmetics Act is the only other toothpaste-specific instrument. The toothpaste tier exists because a dentifrice is applied to the oral mucosa and is partly swallowed, which is the same exposure pattern every formulated row in this category shares. The binding German value carries register status 'guidance impurity limit' (BVL technically-avoidable-content table, the basis on which German competent authorities object to a cosmetic under Regulation (EC) 1223/2009 Article 17) while the Washington toothpaste lead value carries status 'statutory limit' at 1000 ug/kg. HMTc adopts the stricter of the two and discloses both in the candidate set; the selection is not a status judgement and does not depend on one.

Cd.label: The BVL toothpaste cadmium tier (0.1 mg/kg) binds. It is identical to the BVL general-cosmetic cadmium value, so for cadmium the oral tier adds no additional stringency; it is thirty times stricter than the next-strictest surveyed sovereign value (Health Canada and Thailand, 3 mg/kg).
Cd.basis_label: finished dentifrice as placed on market (total cadmium content, ug/kg as sold)
Cd.substantiation: Cadmium reaches dentifrices through mineral abrasives, phosphate raw materials and colour pigments. Eleven sovereign finished-cosmetic instruments were surveyed and are named in the candidate set; the German value binds by a factor of thirty.

tAs.label: The BVL toothpaste total-arsenic tier (0.5 mg/kg) binds, identical to the BVL general-cosmetic value and four times stricter than the next-strictest surveyed sovereign value (Kenya KS 2937 and China NMPA 2015, 2 mg/kg).
tAs.basis_label: finished dentifrice as placed on market (total arsenic content, ug/kg as sold)
tAs.substantiation: This is a TOTAL-arsenic value. It does not satisfy the inorganic-arsenic cell and is not satisfied by an inorganic-arsenic determination; inorganic arsenic is separately controlled by reflex speciation on the iAs cell and is bounded by this value by identity.

control.rationale: Inorganic arsenic is the toxic fraction of total arsenic. No jurisdiction sets an inorganic-arsenic content limit for any oral-care product: every sovereign arsenic value in the cosmetic instrument family (Germany BVL 2017, Health Canada, China NMPA 2015, Korea MFDS, Taiwan MOHW, ASEAN and its national transpositions, Kenya KS 2937, EAEU TR CU 009/2011) is a TOTAL-arsenic value, and every sovereign inorganic-arsenic maximum level is scoped to rice, fish or fruit juice. The cell is therefore held under reflex speciation rather than given an invented ceiling; inorganic arsenic cannot exceed total arsenic by identity, so the published total-arsenic value (500 ug/kg) is its upper bound.
control.reference_method: Reflex HPLC-ICP-MS inorganic-arsenic speciation on any lot whose total-arsenic screen exceeds 50% of the published total-arsenic value. The inorganic fraction is held under ALARA against the tightest available context and any unexplained inorganic arsenic triggers supplier corrective action on the abrasive, clay, mineral-pigment or botanical-extract input that carries it.

tHg.label: The BVL toothpaste total-mercury tier (0.1 mg/kg) binds, identical to the BVL general-cosmetic value and ten times stricter than the near-universal 1 mg/kg cosmetic mercury allowance (US FDA 21 CFR 700.13, Health Canada, China, Korea, Taiwan, ASEAN and its transpositions, India, EAEU).
tHg.basis_label: finished dentifrice as placed on market (total mercury content, ug/kg as sold)
tHg.substantiation: This is a TOTAL-mercury value and it bounds the methylmercury cell by identity. The US instrument named in the candidate set, 21 CFR 700.13, is a binding adulteration rule rather than a guidance figure; it is ten times looser than the German value and does not bind.

not_material.rationale: Methylmercury is formed by microbial methylation in aquatic systems and bioaccumulates in fish muscle. A dentifrice, rinse, whitening or denture-care matrix has no methylating microbial community and no marine input; the mercury sources that reach this category are mineral-abrasive, clay and pigment impurities, which are inorganic. Methylmercury is a species of total mercury and cannot exceed it (MeHg <= tHg), so any mercury present is governed by and bounded by the published total-mercury ceiling of 100 ug/kg on this row.
not_material.reference_method: Total-mercury screen by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2) with ICP-MS determination, reported as ug/kg of product as sold or CV-AAS. No separate methylmercury determination is required for an oral-care matrix; any lot above 50% of the total-mercury ceiling is investigated to its mercury source before release.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No jurisdiction sets a methylmercury limit for any oral-care or cosmetic product. Every sovereign methylmercury maximum level in the register is scoped to fish and seafood. The applicable oral-care mercury instrument (Germany BVL 2017 toothpaste tier, 100 ug/kg) is a TOTAL-mercury value, and it bounds methylmercury by identity.
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: Germany BVL 2017 (toothpaste and general-cosmetic tiers); US FDA 21 CFR 700.13; Washington State Toxics-Free Cosmetics Act; Health Canada Guidance on Heavy Metal Impurities in Cosmetics; China NMPA 2015 Safety and Technical Standards; Korea MFDS Notice 2024-9 and Notice 2025-63; Taiwan MOHW 2024; ASEAN Cosmetic Directive 2019 and the Indonesian (BPOM 16/2024), Malaysian (NPRA 2022), Singaporean (HSA 2024) and Thai transpositions; India Cosmetics Rules 2020; Kenya KS 2937:2021; EAEU TR CU 009/2011 — none sets a methylmercury value.

read_across.label: No sovereign names nickel in an oral-care product. Korea MFDS Notice 2024-9 Article 6(2) is the only instrument in the register that sets a finished-cosmetic nickel content limit at all, and it tiers it by product type: eye makeup 35 ug/g, colour cosmetics 30 ug/g, and all other cosmetics 10 ug/g. An oral-care product is neither eye makeup nor a colour cosmetic, so the residual 'other cosmetics' tier — the STRICTEST of the three — is the nearest applicable sovereign cell and is read across. HMTc does not use the looser makeup tiers.
read_across.substantiation: Nickel is a mucosal and contact sensitiser and reaches oral-care formulations through hydrated-silica and calcium-carbonate abrasives, mineral pigments, and stainless-steel process contact, so the cell must not be left without a ceiling where a sovereign anchor exists. The exact cell (nickel in a dentifrice, rinse, whitening system or denture-care product) is unregulated in every jurisdiction surveyed, which is why the value is published as a disclosed read-across tagged 'read-across' and not as regulatory alignment. Korea MFDS Notice No. 2025-63 restates the same three-tier nickel allowance at the same values; the 2024-9 row is named as the anchor because its register note reproduces the source unit without ambiguity.

Ni.basis_label: finished oral-care product as placed on market (total nickel content, ug/kg as sold) — read across from the Korean residual finished-cosmetic nickel tier

control.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a tin content limit for any oral-care or cosmetic product; the sovereign tin maximum levels in the register are canned-food and food-contact values written for tinplate migration into food and are a different basis entirely. Tin is additionally not a pure impurity in this category: stannous fluoride and stannous chloride are authorised anticaries and antigingivitis actives in dentifrices and mouthrinses, so a finished-product tin ceiling would be exceeded by design in a compliant stannous formulation and would be meaningless as a contaminant control. The cell is held under mandatory analytical control with a declaration reconciliation rather than declared not-material, because tin is unambiguously present at material levels in this category and an absence claim would be contradicted on its face.
control.reference_method: Mandatory per-lot total-tin analysis by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2) with ICP-MS determination, reported as ug/kg of product as sold, reconciled against the batch record's declared stannous input. Tin in excess of the stoichiometric contribution of the declared stannous active, or any quantifiable tin in a product with no declared tin-bearing ingredient, triggers supplier corrective action under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule (ALARA against the tightest available context). No numeric ceiling is published.

control.rationale: No jurisdiction sets an aluminium content limit for any oral-care or cosmetic product. Aluminium is also frequently an intentional, declared functional ingredient in this category rather than a contaminant: hydrated alumina and aluminium oxide are conventional dentifrice abrasives, aluminium hydroxide is a common excipient, and aluminium lakes are the substrate of most permitted cosmetic colours. A finished-product aluminium ceiling would therefore be exceeded by design in a compliant alumina-abrasive formulation. The cell is held under mandatory analytical control with a declaration reconciliation rather than declared not-material, because aluminium is unambiguously present at material levels in this category.
control.reference_method: Mandatory per-lot total-aluminium analysis by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2) with ICP-MS determination, reported as ug/kg of product as sold (ICP-OES permitted where a high-alumina abrasive system saturates the ICP-MS working range), reconciled against the batch record's declared aluminium-bearing ingredients. Aluminium beyond the declared ingredient contribution triggers supplier corrective action on the abrasive, clay or pigment input under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule. No numeric ceiling is published.

control.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a total-chromium content limit for any oral-care or cosmetic product; the only chromium values reachable from this category are the EU toy-migration figures, which are a leachate basis and are excluded by this row's basis guard. Total chromium is in any case a screen rather than a protective ceiling, since it is dominated by benign Cr(III) while the health-relevant species is Cr(VI). The cell is held under mandatory analytical control feeding the Cr(VI) reflex below, and no number is invented.
control.reference_method: Mandatory per-lot total-chromium analysis by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2) with ICP-MS determination, reported as ug/kg of product as sold. Total chromium is used as the screen that triggers the Cr(VI) reflex; any result above the analytical reporting limit that cannot be traced to a declared Cr(III) pigment or to stainless-steel process contact is escalated to supplier corrective action.

control.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a hexavalent-chromium content limit for any oral-care or cosmetic product. Cr(VI) is deliberately NOT registered as a method-artifact not-material determination in this category: the method-artifact basis rests on Cr(VI) reducing to Cr(III) in the matrix, and oral-care matrices routinely contain oxidising systems — hydrogen peroxide and carbamide peroxide whiteners, sodium percarbonate and persulfate denture cleansers, peroxide-containing rinses — in which that reduction cannot be assumed. The cell is a control with a reflex speciation and a zero-tolerance disposition.
control.reference_method: Reflex Cr(VI) speciation on any elevated total-chromium screen: alkaline extraction per EPA 3060A with IC-ICP-MS determination per EPA 6800, or EN 15192 for solid and paste matrices. Any quantifiable Cr(VI) fails the lot and blocks release pending supplier corrective action.

mouthwash-oral-rinse.name: Mouthwash/oral rinse
mouthwash-oral-rinse.native_basis: finished oral rinse as placed on market (total content, ug/kg as sold)
mouthwash-oral-rinse.native_basis_label: finished oral-care product as placed on market — total heavy-metal content per unit mass of product as sold (ug/kg). Not a dietary maximum level and not a migration/leachate value.
mouthwash-oral-rinse.scope_note: Mouthwashes, oral rinses, pre-rinses and concentrated rinses intended to be swished in the oral cavity and expectorated, whether marketed as cosmetics or under an OTC drug monograph (antigingivitis, anticaries fluoride rinse) — the taxonomy routes by exposure pathway, not classification. A fluoride mouthwash is Oral Care and not a dietary supplement, and a whitening mouthwash carrying no drug claim is Oral Care and not a rinse-off cosmetic (taxonomy boundary rules 2 and 3). The product is sold by volume but the standard is expressed per unit MASS of product as sold; a laboratory reporting per litre must convert using the measured density, and no volumetric shortcut is accepted. No reconstitution or dilution conversion is applied: a concentrated rinse is assessed as sold, not as diluted for use.

That boundary is drawn deliberately rather than by silently importing a food maximum level into a cosmetic row, and it is drawn in the protective direction: the relevant US instrument for a hard candy likely to be frequently consumed by small children (FDA lead action level for candy, 100 ug/kg) is five times STRICTER than this row's lead value, so parking a confectionery mint on this row would have certified it against a looser ceiling than its own instrument family requires.

read_across.label: The exact cell is unregulated: no sovereign publishes a lead value for this product form. control.rationale: Inorganic arsenic is the toxic fraction of total arsenic. not_material.rationale: Methylmercury is formed by microbial methylation in aquatic systems and bioaccumulates in fish muscle. read_across.label: No sovereign names nickel in an oral-care product. Korea MFDS Notice No. 2025-63 restates the same three-tier nickel allowance at the same values; the 2024-9 row is named as the anchor because its register note reproduces the source unit without ambiguity.

toothbrushes.native_basis_label: oral-care article as placed on market — total heavy-metal content of each accessible part, per unit mass of that component's material (ug/kg). Not a cosmetic finished-product basis, not a dietary maximum level, and not an EN 71-3 migration/leachate value.
toothbrushes.scope_note: Manual toothbrushes, electric and sonic brush heads, interdental and denture brushes, and children's toothbrushes for ages 6 and over (ages 0-5 route to Category 2). A toothbrush is an ARTICLE, not a cosmetic: a finished-cosmetic contaminant limit is written for a formulated product measured per unit mass of product and does not reach a polymer filament or a stainless-steel staple, so no cosmetic value is used on this row. The applicable instrument is the article-scoped mouth-contact lead ceiling; every other analyte is held under component-level control. The electric handle, charger and dock are outside the certified article; the brush head and any part of the handle that the mouth can reach in normal use are inside it.
toothbrushes.basis_guard: ^(?!.*(cosmetic|migration|leachate|colourant|colorant|surface coating|sticker|as consumed|wet weight|candy))(?=.*(content in accessible part|concentration by weight in article))
toothbrushes.basis_guard_note: An oral-care article is not a cosmetic and is not a food. The guard admits only article material-content instruments (Canada SOR/2018-83 accessible-part lead content; REACH Annex XVII entry 63(7) lead concentration by weight in a mouthable article) and rejects (a) finished-cosmetic impurity limits, which are written for a formulated product and cannot be applied to a polymer filament or a stainless-steel staple, (b) EN 71-3 / Directive 2009/48 toy values, which are MIGRATION limits and would understate content by orders of magnitude if read as content, and (c) surface-coating and sticker instruments, which govern an applied film rather than the substrate.

Pb.label: Canada's Consumer Products Containing Lead Regulations (SOR/2018-83) reach mouth-contact consumer products, and section 2(1) caps EACH ACCESSIBLE PART of such a product at 90 mg/kg total lead. An oral-care article is a consumer product brought into contact with the user's mouth in the course of normal use, so the Canadian value directly regulates this cell on the article's own content basis. The only other article-scoped sovereign lead CONTENT instrument in the register, REACH Annex XVII entry 63(7) as added by Regulation (EU) 2015/628, sets 0.05% lead by weight (500 mg/kg) for articles that may be placed in the mouth by children; it is five and a half times looser and does not bind.
Pb.basis_label: total lead content per accessible part, ug/kg of that component's material (article content basis, not migration)
Pb.substantiation: The Canadian ceiling is applied to every accessible part of the finished article, not to a composite of the whole product, because that is how section 2(1) is written; a composite-averaged result would dilute a leaded component against inert bulk and is not accepted. Components tested separately: bristle/filament tuft, the metal staple or anchor wire that retains the tuft, the handle polymer, any elastomeric overmould or grip, any pad-printed or in-mould graphic, and for electric brush heads the shaft, the drive coupling and any plated or metal part. The tuft-retaining staple and any plated part are sampled as separate components because they are the most likely leaded and nickel-bearing parts of the article and would be invisible in a whole-brush composite. Two allowances written into the cited instruments are deliberately NOT taken: SOR/2018-83 section 2(2)'s conditional essential-characteristic exception, which substitutes a release criterion for the content criterion, and the REACH entry 63(8)(g) brass-alloy derogation at 0.5% lead by weight. Both are machinability and functional-necessity allowances rather than health findings, and HMTc certifies against the content criterion without them. The EU toy values (Directive 2009/48 / EN 71-3) are likewise not used: they are migration limits on a leachate basis, and reading a migration number as a content ceiling is the basis conflation this row's guard exists to prevent.

control.rationale: No sovereign sets a cadmium content limit for a mouth-contact oral-care article. Canada's Consumer Products Containing Lead Regulations (SOR/2018-83), the only instrument that reaches this product form on a total-content basis, is lead-only; the EU toy values (Directive 2009/48 / EN 71-3) are MIGRATION limits and are excluded by this row's basis guard, and finished-cosmetic impurity schedules are written for a formulated product and do not reach an article. The cell is held under mandatory analytical control, not declared not-material: cadmium is a known pigment and polymer-stabiliser residue in coloured plastics and a plating-bath contaminant, both of which are present in this article class.
control.reference_method: Mandatory per-lot total-content analysis by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2) with ICP-MS determination, reported as ug/kg of product as sold, with COMPONENT-LEVEL sampling of the finished article (bristle/filament tuft, the metal staple or anchor wire that retains the tuft, the handle polymer, any elastomeric overmould or grip, any pad-printed or in-mould graphic, and for electric brush heads the shaft, the drive coupling and any plated or metal part) — each component digested and reported separately, with no composite-averaged result accepted. No numeric ceiling is published; results are dispositioned under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule (ALARA against the tightest available context plus supplier corrective action on the identified component).

The cell is held under mandatory analytical control, not declared not-material: aluminium is a structural and pigment-substrate constituent of this article class rather than a trace impurity, so an absence claim is not available.
control.reference_method: Mandatory per-lot total-content analysis by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2) with ICP-MS determination, reported as ug/kg of product as sold, with COMPONENT-LEVEL sampling of the finished article (the jet tip and nozzle, the tip polymer and any metal insert, the handle body, the accessible housing, and every wetted water-path component (reservoir, tubing, seals, pump wetted parts)) — each component digested and reported separately, with no composite-averaged result accepted. No numeric ceiling is published; results are dispositioned under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule (ALARA against the tightest available context plus supplier corrective action on the identified component).

control.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a hexavalent-chromium CONTENT limit for a consumer article; the EU toy figure (Directive 2009/48 Category II, 5 ug/kg) is a migration value on a leachate basis and cannot be read as a content ceiling without conflating the two, which this row's basis guard forbids. Cr(VI) is not registered as a method artifact here: chrome-plated and chromate-passivated metal parts, stainless-steel filament staples and orthodontic-grade wire are real Cr(VI) sources in mouth-contact articles, so an absence claim would not survive the substantiation gate. The cell is a control with reflex speciation and a zero-tolerance disposition.
control.reference_method: Reflex Cr(VI) speciation (EPA 3060A alkaline extraction with IC-ICP-MS per EPA 6800, or EN 15192) on any component (the jet tip and nozzle, the tip polymer and any metal insert, the handle body, the accessible housing, and every wetted water-path component (reservoir, tubing, seals, pump wetted parts)) returning an elevated total-chromium screen. Any quantifiable Cr(VI) fails the lot and blocks release pending supplier corrective action.

whitening-products.name: Whitening products (strips/gels/powders/pens)
whitening-products.native_basis: finished tooth-whitening product as placed on market (total content, ug/kg as sold)
whitening-products.native_basis_label: finished oral-care product as placed on market — total heavy-metal content per unit mass of product as sold (ug/kg). Not a dietary maximum level and not a migration/leachate value.
whitening-products.scope_note: Dedicated tooth-whitening systems: peroxide strips, whitening gels and tray gels, whitening pens, and non-dentifrice whitening powders (activated-charcoal and clay-based powders). Tooth-whitening products containing hydrogen or carbamide peroxide are cosmetics in the EU (Regulation 1223/2009 Annex III entry 12) and the finished-cosmetic contaminant instruments are the applicable family. A whitening claim on a conventional toothpaste keeps that product in the dentifrices row; a whitening mouthrinse with no drug claim may be certified on either this row or the mouthwash row, and both carry identical values so the routing choice cannot change the outcome. Clay- and charcoal-based whitening powders are the highest-risk form in this row: mineral raw materials carry lead, arsenic and chromium, and the EAEU natural-plant-or-mineral-raw-material cosmetic tier (named in the candidate sets) is the instrument written for exactly that composition — it is looser than the binding German value and therefore does not bind.

whitening-products.basis_guard_note: Every named anchor on a formulated oral row must be a FINISHED-COSMETIC (or finished oral-product) total-content instrument. The guard rejects three families that would otherwise conflate bases: colour-additive and ingredient purity specifications (21 CFR 73/74, the India permitted-colours entry), which cap one raw material and not the finished product; migration/leachate values (EN 71-3 / Directive 2009/48 toy migration, food-contact migration), which measure release rather than content; and dietary maximum levels expressed as-consumed or wet weight. A basis failure resolves the cell to a GAP and fails the build rather than publishing a number in the wrong basis.

read_across.label: The exact cell is unregulated: no sovereign publishes a lead value for this product form. Germany BVL 2017's toothpaste tier (0.5 mg/kg) is the nearest applicable sovereign cell because it is the only sovereign lead value written for a product applied to the oral mucosa and partly swallowed, which is this form's exposure pattern. The directly applicable German general-cosmetic tier is 2 mg/kg; HMTc reads the stricter oral tier across rather than taking the looser general value, and discloses that choice here rather than presenting the number as direct regulatory alignment.
read_across.substantiation: This is the Category 15 precedent applied to its home matrix: the BVL toothpaste tier was read across to mucosal-contact products in the live Feminine Care standard on the reasoning that oral mucosa is the closest regulated analogue to other mucosa. Here the analogy is tighter still, because the target form is itself an oral-cavity product. The read-across moves the value DOWN from the directly applicable general-cosmetic tier (2000 to 500 ug/kg), so it cannot be characterised as a convenience selection.

Pb.basis_label: finished oral-care product as placed on market (total lead content, ug/kg as sold) — read across from the Germany BVL 2017 toothpaste tier

Cd.label: The German BVL general-cosmetic cadmium value (0.1 mg/kg) directly regulates this form and binds. It is identical to the BVL toothpaste tier, so for cadmium the oral read-across would produce the same number and is not needed.
Cd.basis_label: finished oral-care product as placed on market (total cadmium content, ug/kg as sold)
Cd.substantiation: Ten sovereign finished-cosmetic instruments are named in the candidate set; the German value binds by a factor of thirty over the next strictest (Health Canada and Thailand, 3 mg/kg).

tAs.label: The German BVL general-cosmetic total-arsenic value (0.5 mg/kg) directly regulates this form and binds. It is identical to the BVL toothpaste tier, so the oral read-across would produce the same number.
tAs.basis_label: finished oral-care product as placed on market (total arsenic content, ug/kg as sold)
tAs.substantiation: TOTAL arsenic. It neither satisfies nor is satisfied by the inorganic-arsenic cell, which is separately controlled by reflex speciation and bounded by this value.

control.rationale: Inorganic arsenic is the toxic fraction of total arsenic. No jurisdiction sets an inorganic-arsenic content limit for any oral-care product: every sovereign arsenic value in the cosmetic instrument family (Germany BVL 2017, Health Canada, China NMPA 2015, Korea MFDS, Taiwan MOHW, ASEAN and its national transpositions, Kenya KS 2937, EAEU TR CU 009/2011) is a TOTAL-arsenic value, and every sovereign inorganic-arsenic maximum level is scoped to rice, fish or fruit juice. The cell is therefore held under reflex speciation rather than given an invented ceiling; inorganic arsenic cannot exceed total arsenic by identity, so the published total-arsenic value (500 ug/kg) is its upper bound.
control.reference_method: Reflex HPLC-ICP-MS inorganic-arsenic speciation on any lot whose total-arsenic screen exceeds 50% of the published total-arsenic value. The inorganic fraction is held under ALARA against the tightest available context and any unexplained inorganic arsenic triggers supplier corrective action on the abrasive, clay, mineral-pigment or botanical-extract input that carries it.

tHg.label: The German BVL general-cosmetic total-mercury value (0.1 mg/kg) directly regulates this form and binds. It is identical to the BVL toothpaste tier, and ten times stricter than the near-universal 1 mg/kg cosmetic mercury allowance.
tHg.basis_label: finished oral-care product as placed on market (total mercury content, ug/kg as sold)
tHg.substantiation: TOTAL mercury; it bounds the methylmercury cell by identity.

not_material.rationale: Methylmercury is formed by microbial methylation in aquatic systems and bioaccumulates in fish muscle. A dentifrice, rinse, whitening or denture-care matrix has no methylating microbial community and no marine input; the mercury sources that reach this category are mineral-abrasive, clay and pigment impurities, which are inorganic. Methylmercury is a species of total mercury and cannot exceed it (MeHg <= tHg), so any mercury present is governed by and bounded by the published total-mercury ceiling of 100 ug/kg on this row.
not_material.reference_method: Total-mercury screen by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2) with ICP-MS determination, reported as ug/kg of product as sold or CV-AAS. No separate methylmercury determination is required for an oral-care matrix; any lot above 50% of the total-mercury ceiling is investigated to its mercury source before release.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No jurisdiction sets a methylmercury limit for any oral-care or cosmetic product. Every sovereign methylmercury maximum level in the register is scoped to fish and seafood. The applicable oral-care mercury instrument (Germany BVL 2017 toothpaste tier, 100 ug/kg) is a TOTAL-mercury value, and it bounds methylmercury by identity.
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: Germany BVL 2017 (toothpaste and general-cosmetic tiers); US FDA 21 CFR 700.13; Washington State Toxics-Free Cosmetics Act; Health Canada Guidance on Heavy Metal Impurities in Cosmetics; China NMPA 2015 Safety and Technical Standards; Korea MFDS Notice 2024-9 and Notice 2025-63; Taiwan MOHW 2024; ASEAN Cosmetic Directive 2019 and the Indonesian (BPOM 16/2024), Malaysian (NPRA 2022), Singaporean (HSA 2024) and Thai transpositions; India Cosmetics Rules 2020; Kenya KS 2937:2021; EAEU TR CU 009/2011 — none sets a methylmercury value.

read_across.label: No sovereign names nickel in an oral-care product. Korea MFDS Notice 2024-9 Article 6(2) is the only instrument in the register that sets a finished-cosmetic nickel content limit at all, and it tiers it by product type: eye makeup 35 ug/g, colour cosmetics 30 ug/g, and all other cosmetics 10 ug/g. An oral-care product is neither eye makeup nor a colour cosmetic, so the residual 'other cosmetics' tier — the STRICTEST of the three — is the nearest applicable sovereign cell and is read across. HMTc does not use the looser makeup tiers.
read_across.substantiation: Nickel is a mucosal and contact sensitiser and reaches oral-care formulations through hydrated-silica and calcium-carbonate abrasives, mineral pigments, and stainless-steel process contact, so the cell must not be left without a ceiling where a sovereign anchor exists. The exact cell (nickel in a dentifrice, rinse, whitening system or denture-care product) is unregulated in every jurisdiction surveyed, which is why the value is published as a disclosed read-across tagged 'read-across' and not as regulatory alignment. Korea MFDS Notice No. 2025-63 restates the same three-tier nickel allowance at the same values; the 2024-9 row is named as the anchor because its register note reproduces the source unit without ambiguity.

Ni.basis_label: finished oral-care product as placed on market (total nickel content, ug/kg as sold) — read across from the Korean residual finished-cosmetic nickel tier

control.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a tin content limit for any oral-care or cosmetic product; the sovereign tin maximum levels in the register are canned-food and food-contact values written for tinplate migration into food and are a different basis entirely. Tin is additionally not a pure impurity in this category: stannous fluoride and stannous chloride are authorised anticaries and antigingivitis actives in dentifrices and mouthrinses, so a finished-product tin ceiling would be exceeded by design in a compliant stannous formulation and would be meaningless as a contaminant control. The cell is held under mandatory analytical control with a declaration reconciliation rather than declared not-material, because tin is unambiguously present at material levels in this category and an absence claim would be contradicted on its face.
control.reference_method: Mandatory per-lot total-tin analysis by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2) with ICP-MS determination, reported as ug/kg of product as sold, reconciled against the batch record's declared stannous input. Tin in excess of the stoichiometric contribution of the declared stannous active, or any quantifiable tin in a product with no declared tin-bearing ingredient, triggers supplier corrective action under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule (ALARA against the tightest available context). No numeric ceiling is published.

control.rationale: No jurisdiction sets an aluminium content limit for any oral-care or cosmetic product. Aluminium is also frequently an intentional, declared functional ingredient in this category rather than a contaminant: hydrated alumina and aluminium oxide are conventional dentifrice abrasives, aluminium hydroxide is a common excipient, and aluminium lakes are the substrate of most permitted cosmetic colours. A finished-product aluminium ceiling would therefore be exceeded by design in a compliant alumina-abrasive formulation. The cell is held under mandatory analytical control with a declaration reconciliation rather than declared not-material, because aluminium is unambiguously present at material levels in this category.
control.reference_method: Mandatory per-lot total-aluminium analysis by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2) with ICP-MS determination, reported as ug/kg of product as sold (ICP-OES permitted where a high-alumina abrasive system saturates the ICP-MS working range), reconciled against the batch record's declared aluminium-bearing ingredients. Aluminium beyond the declared ingredient contribution triggers supplier corrective action on the abrasive, clay or pigment input under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule. No numeric ceiling is published.

control.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a total-chromium content limit for any oral-care or cosmetic product; the only chromium values reachable from this category are the EU toy-migration figures, which are a leachate basis and are excluded by this row's basis guard. Total chromium is in any case a screen rather than a protective ceiling, since it is dominated by benign Cr(III) while the health-relevant species is Cr(VI). The cell is held under mandatory analytical control feeding the Cr(VI) reflex below, and no number is invented.
control.reference_method: Mandatory per-lot total-chromium analysis by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2) with ICP-MS determination, reported as ug/kg of product as sold. Total chromium is used as the screen that triggers the Cr(VI) reflex; any result above the analytical reporting limit that cannot be traced to a declared Cr(III) pigment or to stainless-steel process contact is escalated to supplier corrective action.

control.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a hexavalent-chromium content limit for any oral-care or cosmetic product. Cr(VI) is deliberately NOT registered as a method-artifact not-material determination in this category: the method-artifact basis rests on Cr(VI) reducing to Cr(III) in the matrix, and oral-care matrices routinely contain oxidising systems — hydrogen peroxide and carbamide peroxide whiteners, sodium percarbonate and persulfate denture cleansers, peroxide-containing rinses — in which that reduction cannot be assumed. The cell is a control with a reflex speciation and a zero-tolerance disposition.
control.reference_method: Reflex Cr(VI) speciation on any elevated total-chromium screen: alkaline extraction per EPA 3060A with IC-ICP-MS determination per EPA 6800, or EN 15192 for solid and paste matrices. Any quantifiable Cr(VI) fails the lot and blocks release pending supplier corrective action.

tongue-cleaners-scrapers.name: Tongue cleaners/scrapers
tongue-cleaners-scrapers.native_basis: oral-care article as placed on market (total content per accessible part, ug/kg)
tongue-cleaners-scrapers.native_basis_label: oral-care article as placed on market — total heavy-metal content of each accessible part, per unit mass of that component's material (ug/kg). Not a cosmetic finished-product basis, not a dietary maximum level, and not an EN 71-3 migration/leachate value.
tongue-cleaners-scrapers.scope_note: Tongue scrapers and cleaners in stainless steel, copper and copper-alloy, and polymer, and the tongue-cleaning face moulded onto some toothbrush heads (which is certified with the brush on the toothbrushes row). These are ARTICLES and no cosmetic finished-product contaminant limit reaches them. Copper-alloy scrapers are the highest-risk form in the row: leaded brasses and bronzes are common in low-cost cast and machined copper articles, and REACH's brass derogation at 0.5% lead by weight is explicitly NOT used here — the Canadian 90 mg/kg accessible-part ceiling is applied to copper-alloy scrapers without derogation, because the derogation is a machinability allowance rather than a health finding.
tongue-cleaners-scrapers.basis_guard: ^(?!.*(cosmetic|migration|leachate|colourant|colorant|surface coating|sticker|as consumed|wet weight|candy))(?=.*(content in accessible part|concentration by weight in article))
tongue-cleaners-scrapers.basis_guard_note: An oral-care article is not a cosmetic and is not a food. The guard admits only article material-content instruments (Canada SOR/2018-83 accessible-part lead content; REACH Annex XVII entry 63(7) lead concentration by weight in a mouthable article) and rejects (a) finished-cosmetic impurity limits, which are written for a formulated product and cannot be applied to a polymer filament or a stainless-steel staple, (b) EN 71-3 / Directive 2009/48 toy values, which are MIGRATION limits and would understate content by orders of magnitude if read as content, and (c) surface-coating and sticker instruments, which govern an applied film rather than the substrate.

Pb.label: Canada's Consumer Products Containing Lead Regulations (SOR/2018-83) reach mouth-contact consumer products, and section 2(1) caps EACH ACCESSIBLE PART of such a product at 90 mg/kg total lead. An oral-care article is a consumer product brought into contact with the user's mouth in the course of normal use, so the Canadian value directly regulates this cell on the article's own content basis. The only other article-scoped sovereign lead CONTENT instrument in the register, REACH Annex XVII entry 63(7) as added by Regulation (EU) 2015/628, sets 0.05% lead by weight (500 mg/kg) for articles that may be placed in the mouth by children; it is five and a half times looser and does not bind.
Pb.basis_label: total lead content per accessible part, ug/kg of that component's material (article content basis, not migration)
Pb.substantiation: The Canadian ceiling is applied to every accessible part of the finished article, not to a composite of the whole product, because that is how section 2(1) is written; a composite-averaged result would dilute a leaded component against inert bulk and is not accepted. Components tested separately: the scraping edge and blade (stainless steel, copper alloy or polymer), the handle or loop, any plating or surface treatment, and any elastomeric grip. The scraping edge is sampled separately from the handle because it is the part in abrasive mucosal contact and, on plated articles, carries the plating chemistry. Two allowances written into the cited instruments are deliberately NOT taken: SOR/2018-83 section 2(2)'s conditional essential-characteristic exception, which substitutes a release criterion for the content criterion, and the REACH entry 63(8)(g) brass-alloy derogation at 0.5% lead by weight. Both are machinability and functional-necessity allowances rather than health findings, and HMTc certifies against the content criterion without them. The EU toy values (Directive 2009/48 / EN 71-3) are likewise not used: they are migration limits on a leachate basis, and reading a migration number as a content ceiling is the basis conflation this row's guard exists to prevent.

control.rationale: No sovereign sets a cadmium content limit for a mouth-contact oral-care article. Canada's Consumer Products Containing Lead Regulations (SOR/2018-83), the only instrument that reaches this product form on a total-content basis, is lead-only; the EU toy values (Directive 2009/48 / EN 71-3) are MIGRATION limits and are excluded by this row's basis guard, and finished-cosmetic impurity schedules are written for a formulated product and do not reach an article. The cell is held under mandatory analytical control, not declared not-material: cadmium is a known pigment and polymer-stabiliser residue in coloured plastics and a plating-bath contaminant, both of which are present in this article class.
control.reference_method: Mandatory per-lot total-content analysis by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2) with ICP-MS determination, reported as ug/kg of product as sold, with COMPONENT-LEVEL sampling of the finished article (the scraping edge and blade (stainless steel, copper alloy or polymer), the handle or loop, any plating or surface treatment, and any elastomeric grip) — each component digested and reported separately, with no composite-averaged result accepted. No numeric ceiling is published; results are dispositioned under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule (ALARA against the tightest available context plus supplier corrective action on the identified component).

Mercury is therefore governed through the total-mercury control.

Methylmercury speciation (GC-ICP-MS, EPA 1630) is required only where a confirmed total-mercury result cannot be traced to an inorganic input.
